reads.note: Nested inside SessionUser.creator, null for account type 'user'. Not independently fetched anywhere in this screen's code — it only arrives embedded in the AuthResponse.user object returned by signUp/verifyOtp/signIn's mock branch. In the mock fallback it is never actually populated (mock SessionUser literals in auth.ts always set creator: null), so this screen never exercises a non-null CreatorState in practice.

actions.name: signUp
actions.note: Mock fallback fabricates wawuId as `wawu_${email local-part}`, sets interests: [], verification: 'basic', creator: null unconditionally regardless of accountType — a creator signup never gets a non-null CreatorState back from this call in mock mode.

actions.name: verifyOtp
actions.note: Mock fallback returns fullName: '' and accountType: 'user' unconditionally; SignUpFlow.tsx immediately overwrites both client-side by spreading otpState (the fullName/accountType captured at signup time) over the response before calling signInUser — i.e. the UI does not trust the mock verify response for these two fields and patches them locally. A real backend response is expected to return the correct fullName/accountType itself.

actions.name: signIn
actions.note: Mock fallback reads any previously-set sessionStorage.getUser() as a fallback identity source before fabricating one — an artifact of pure client-side mock state, not a real contract behavior.

actions.name: saveNewPassword
actions.note: ResetPasswordForm's copy ('You will be signed in on this device once it is saved') implies the real endpoint should also return/establish a session token on success, but the payload/response as coded never sends or returns a token or reset-token/code identifying which account is being reset — the UI has no field capturing a reset token from the emailed link (no [token] route param, no query-string read) anywhere in reset-password/page.tsx. This is a contract gap: the client-side flow cannot actually identify which user's password to change.

authContext.note: This screen is the pre-auth surface itself (sign-in/sign-up/forgot/reset) — no route or component here checks isAuthenticated, creatorGates(), or any role/gate. SignInForm/SignUpFlow/ResetPasswordForm call session-provider's signInUser() to ESTABLISH a session but consume no gated data themselves. Sign-up lets the user pick accountType ('user'|'creator') client-side with no server-side validation visible at this layer; CreatorState fields (subscriptionPaid, kyc) are never read or written by any of these five actions — creator onboarding (a separate screen) owns that.

special.note: OTP resend countdown (resendSeconds, starts at 42) is a pure client-side setInterval timer in SignUpFlow.tsx with no visible resend-OTP API call wired to the 'Resend the code' UI — pressing 'resend' has no handler in the read code (only the countdown display exists); no polling of verification status either. Reset-password flow has no token/code capture from the emailed link at all (see saveNewPassword note above).

designIntentNote: design/screens/WAWU Auth.dc.html's own caption (line 35) states outright: 'Auth stays with WAWU ID — these screens collect and hand off, they do not replace it. ... No ID upload or document capture here; that belongs to creator onboarding.' This matches conventions.md's architecture decision that WAWU ID is a separately-deployed external identity provider and this backend is a pure resource server that never issues its own login/signup/OTP/refresh tokens. The five SEAM-tagged endpoints in src/lib/api/auth.ts (POST /api/hub/auth/signup, /auth/otp/verify, /auth/signin, /auth/reset, /auth/reset/confirm) as currently coded imply this backend itself owns password storage and auth issuance, which conflicts with that architecture — flagging for reconciliation, not resolving here.
